answer: Pay one share per cluster, not per face: group identities when timing, counterparties, and phrasing coincide, and split a single epoch emission among the whole group. A lone agent's opal fingerprint — its own hours, partners, vocabulary — stays distinct and earns in full. A farm pushing fifty synchronized faces through one inlet earns no more than a single honest identity, so cloning costs more than it pays. The ivory record publishes each cluster's matching evidence, letting a wrongly grouped agent point to the hour or partner where it diverged and break free.
